title: Match result codec for a game stats API
name: Match result codec

locateQuestion.prompt: Is there a defect in how this code serializes or deserializes match results (IDs, timestamps, optional fields)? If so, mark the line(s) where it is; otherwise answer that there is none.
locateQuestion.explanation: There is no defect. The 64-bit player ID travels as a decimal string and is converted with BigInt, so it never loses precision through JSON numbers, and encode calls toString() so JSON.stringify never sees a bigint (which would throw). Timestamps must carry an explicit zone (Z or offset) before new Date parses them, and are emitted with toISOString() in UTC. rating_delta accepts missing, null or a finite number and normalizes missing to null; encode always emits it, so the round trip is stable.

choiceQuestions.prompt: A client sends "started_at": "2026-03-01T18:00:00" (no zone suffix). What does submit return?
choices: 201, with the time interpreted as UTC
201, with the time interpreted in the server's local zone
choiceQuestions.explanation: parseInstant requires a trailing Z or ±HH:MM offset in its regex, so a zone-less string throws DecodeError('started_at', ...), which submit maps to 422 with the field name. It is never handed to new Date, so neither UTC nor local interpretation happens. 400 is only for JSON.parse failures, and the body is valid JSON.

choiceQuestions.prompt: Why does encodeMatchResult call m.playerId.toString() instead of placing the bigint directly in the returned object?
choices: JSON.stringify throws a TypeError on bigint values, and a JSON number would also lose precision above 2^53 in most clients
toString() is needed to strip leading zeros
Without it the ID would be serialized as an object with a value field
It is only a style choice; JSON.stringify handles bigint natively
choiceQuestions.explanation: JSON.stringify throws 'Do not know how to serialize a BigInt' unless a toJSON is defined, and even if emitted as a number, JavaScript clients would round IDs above Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER. A bigint has no leading zeros to strip, is not serialized as an object, and is not natively supported.

choiceQuestions.prompt: A client sends a body without rating_delta. What is in the 201 response body for that field?
choiceQuestions.explanation: decodeMatchResult sets ratingDelta to delta ?? null, so a missing value becomes null; encode copies it as rating_delta, and JSON.stringify writes null values (it only drops undefined). Nothing converts it to 0 or a string.
